drivingQuestion: How can a brother who rapes his sister pay a fine if he was subject to being killed as a pursuer?
outcomeNote: Resolutions follow in the next unit.

segments.he: ״חֵטְא״ – אֵלּוּ חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת. וּרְמִינְהוּ: וְאֵלּוּ נְעָרוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן קְנָס – הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ.
segments.en: § The baraita taught that the word «“sin”» is referring to women who are forbidden to a man by a prohibition the violation of which renders him «liable to» receive «karet.» From here it is derived that a man who attempts to rape a woman who is forbidden to him under penalty of karet may be killed. The Gemara «raises a contradiction» between this and what is taught in a mishna (Ketubot 29a): «These are the» cases of «young women for whom there is a fine» paid «to their» fathers by one who rapes them, and the list includes: «One who engages in intercourse with his sister.» One who engages in intercourse with his sister is punished with karet, and accordingly, a woman being raped by her brother may be saved even at the cost of her brother’s life. Whenever one is liable to be killed at the hands of people, even if the transgressor is not killed, the transgressor is exempt from paying any fine or payment. Therefore, since one attempting to rape his sister may be killed, he should be exempt from the fine ordinarily imposed upon a rapist.
